1	# AI Evolution: Research, Industry, and Regulation Datasets
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	Four datasets tracking the parallel development of AI across research, industry adoption, regulation, and private investment from 2010 to 2025.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### research_milestones
     9	15 key research breakthroughs from AlexNet (2012) to frontier models (2025). Each entry has date, label, significance level (medium/high/critical), and a detail description.
    10	
    11	### industry_milestones
    12	13 industry adoption events from Siri (2011) to AI coding agents (2025). Same structure as research milestones.
    13	
    14	### regulation_milestones
    15	13 regulatory and policy events from the Obama AI report (2016) to EU AI Act enforcement (2025). Same structure.
    16	
    17	### ai_investment
    18	Annual global private AI investment in billions USD, 16 data points from 2010 to 2025.
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- Each milestone has a `significance` field: "medium", "high", or "critical"
    22	- All 3 milestone datasets share the same structure (date, label, significance, detail)
    23	- Investment data is annual aggregates from industry reports
    24	- Dates are in YYYY-MM format for milestones, YYYY for investment

1 --- 2 name: mermaidjs-v11 3 description: Create diagrams and visualizations using Mermaid.js v11 syntax. Use when generating flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, ER diagrams, Gantt charts, user journeys, timelines, architecture diagrams, or any of 24+ diagram types. Supports JavaScript API integration, CLI rendering to SVG/PNG/PDF, theming, configuration, and accessibility features. Essential for documentation, technical diagrams, project planning, system architecture, and visual communication. 4 --- 5 6 # Mermaid.js v11 7 8 ## Overview 9 10 Create text-based diagrams using Mermaid.js v11 declarative syntax. Convert code to SVG/PNG/PDF via CLI or render in browsers/markdown files. 11 12 ## Quick Start 13 14 **Basic Diagram Structure:** 15 ``` 16 {diagram-type} 17 {diagram-content} 18 ``` 19 20 **Common Diagram Types:** 21 - `flowchart` - Process flows, decision trees 22 - `sequenceDiagram` - Actor interactions, API flows 23 - `classDiagram` - OOP structures, data models 24 - `stateDiagram` - State machines, workflows 25 - `erDiagram` - Database relationships 26 - `gantt` - Project timelines 27 - `journey` - User experience flows 28 29 See `references/diagram-types.md` for all 24+ types with syntax. 30 31 ## Creating Diagrams 32 33 **Inline Markdown Code Blocks:** 34 ````markdown 35 ```mermaid 36 flowchart TD 37 A[Start] --> B{Decision} 38 B -->|Yes| C[Action] 39 B -->|No| D[End] 40 ``` 41 ```` 42 43 **Configuration via Frontmatter:** 44 ````markdown 45 ```mermaid 46 --- 47 theme: dark 48 --- 49 flowchart LR 50 A --> B 51 ``` 52 ```` 53 54 **Comments:** Use `%% ` prefix for single-line comments. 55 56 ## CLI Usage 57 58 Convert `.mmd` files to images: 59 ```bash 60 # Installation 61 npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 62 63 # Basic conversion 64 mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o diagram.svg 65 66 # With theme and background 67 mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png -t dark -b transparent 68 69 # Custom styling 70 mmdc -i diagram.mmd --cssFile style.css -o output.svg 71 ``` 72 73 See `references/cli-usage.md` for Docker, batch processing, and advanced workflows. 74 75 ## JavaScript Integration 76 77 **HTML Embedding:** 78 ```html 79

83 84 85 ``` 86 87 See `references/integration.md` for Node.js API and advanced integration patterns. 88 89 ## Configuration & Theming 90 91 **Common Options:** 92 - `theme`: "default", "dark", "forest", "neutral", "base" 93 - `look`: "classic", "handDrawn" 94 - `fontFamily`: Custom font specification 95 - `securityLevel`: "strict", "loose", "antiscript" 96 97 See `references/configuration.md` for complete config options, theming, and customization. 98 99 ## Practical Patterns 100 101 Load `references/examples.md` for: 102 - Architecture diagrams 103 - API documentation flows 104 - Database schemas 105 - Project timelines 106 - State machines 107 - User journey maps 108 109 ## Resources 110 111 - `references/diagram-types.md` - Syntax for all 24+ diagram types 112 - `references/configuration.md` - Config, theming, accessibility 113 - `references/cli-usage.md` - CLI commands and workflows 114 - `references/integration.md` - JavaScript API and embedding 115 - `references/examples.md` - Practical patterns and use cases

1	# Mermaid.js Diagram Types
     2	
     3	Comprehensive syntax reference for all 24+ diagram types in Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Core Diagrams
     6	
     7	### Flowchart
     8	Process flows, decision trees, workflows.
     9	
    10	**Syntax:**
    11	```
    12	flowchart {direction}
    13	  {nodeId}[{label}] {arrow} {nodeId}[{label}]
    14	```
    15	
    16	**Directions:** TB/TD (top-bottom), BT, LR (left-right), RL
    17	**Shapes:** `()` round, `[]` rect, `{}` diamond, `{{}}` hexagon, `(())` circle
    18	**Arrows:** `-->` solid, `-.->` dotted, `==>` thick
    19	**Subgraphs:** Group related nodes
    20	
    21	### Sequence Diagram
    22	Actor interactions, API flows, message sequences.
    23	
    24	**Syntax:**
    25	```
    26	sequenceDiagram
    27	  participant A as Actor
    28	  A->>B: Message
    29	  activate B
    30	  B-->>A: Response
    31	  deactivate B
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Arrows:** `->` solid, `->>` arrow, `-->` dotted, `-x` cross, `-)` async
    35	**Features:** Loops, alternatives, parallel, optional, critical regions
    36	
    37	### Class Diagram
    38	OOP structures, inheritance, relationships.
    39	
    40	**Syntax:**
    41	```
    42	classDiagram
    43	  class Animal {
    44	    +String name
    45	    -int age
    46	    +void eat()
    47	  }
    48	  Animal <|-- Dog : inherits
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Visibility:** `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package
    52	**Relationships:** `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->` association
    53	
    54	### State Diagram
    55	State machines, transitions, workflows.
    56	
    57	**Syntax:**
    58	```
    59	stateDiagram-v2
    60	  [*] --> State1
    61	  State1 --> State2 : transition
    62	  State2 --> [*]
    63	```
    64	
    65	**Features:** Composite states, choice points, forks/joins, concurrency
    66	
    67	### ER Diagram
    68	Database relationships, schemas.
    69	
    70	**Syntax:**
    71	```
    72	erDiagram
    73	  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    74	  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
    75	```
    76	
    77	**Cardinality:** `||` one, `|o` zero-one, `}|` one-many, `}o` zero-many
    78	
    79	## Planning Diagrams
    80	
    81	### Gantt Chart
    82	Project timelines, schedules.
    83	
    84	**Syntax:**
    85	```
    86	gantt
    87	  title Project
    88	  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    89	  section Phase1
    90	    Task1 :done, 2024-01-01, 5d
    91	    Task2 :active, after Task1, 3d
    92	```
    93	
    94	**Status:** `done`, `active`, `crit`, `milestone`
    95	
    96	### User Journey
    97	Experience flows, satisfaction tracking.
    98	
    99	**Syntax:**
   100	```
   101	journey
   102	  title User Journey
   103	  section Shopping
   104	    Browse: 5: Customer
   105	    Add to cart: 3: Customer, System
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Scores:** 1-5 satisfaction levels
   109	
   110	### Kanban
   111	Task boards, workflow stages.
   112	
   113	**Syntax:**
   114	```
   115	kanban
   116	  Todo[Task Board]
   117	    task1[Implement API]
   118	    @{ assigned: "Dev1", priority: "High" }
   119	  InProgress[In Progress]
   120	    task2[Fix bug]
   121	```
   122	
   123	### Quadrant Chart
   124	Prioritization, trend analysis.
   125	
   126	**Syntax:**
   127	```
   128	quadrantChart
   129	  x-axis Low --> High
   130	  y-axis Low --> High
   131	  Item A: [0.3, 0.6]
   132	```
   133	
   134	## Architecture Diagrams
   135	
   136	### C4 Diagram
   137	System architecture, components.
   138	
   139	**Syntax:**
   140	```
   141	C4Context
   142	  Person(user, "User")
   143	  System(app, "Application")
   144	  Rel(user, app, "Uses")
   145	```
   146	
   147	### Architecture Diagram
   148	Cloud infrastructure, services.
   149	
   150	**Syntax:**
   151	```
   152	architecture-beta
   153	  service api(server)[API]
   154	  service db(database)[Database]
   155	  api:R --> L:db
   156	```
   157	
   158	**Icons:** cloud, database, disk, internet, server, or iconify.design icons
   159	
   160	### Block Diagram
   161	Module dependencies, networks.
   162	
   163	**Syntax:**
   164	```
   165	block-beta
   166	  columns 3
   167	  a["Block A"] b["Block B"]
   168	  a --> b
   169	```
   170	
   171	**Shapes:** rounded, stadium, cylinder, diamond, trapezoid, hexagon
   172	
   173	## Data Visualization
   174	
   175	### Pie Chart
   176	Proportions, distributions.
   177	
   178	**Syntax:**
   179	```
   180	pie showData
   181	  "Category A" : 45.5
   182	  "Category B" : 30.0
   183	```
   184	
   185	### XY Chart
   186	Trends, comparisons.
   187	
   188	**Syntax:**
   189	```
   190	xychart-beta
   191	  x-axis [jan, feb, mar]
   192	  y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100
   193	  line [30, 45, 60]
   194	  bar [25, 40, 55]
   195	```
   196	
   197	### Sankey
   198	Flow visualization, resource allocation.
   199	
   200	**Syntax:**
   201	```
   202	sankey-beta
   203	  Source,Target,Value
   204	  A,B,10
   205	  B,C,5
   206	```
   207	
   208	### Radar Chart
   209	Multi-dimensional comparison.
   210	
   211	**Syntax:**
   212	```
   213	radar-beta
   214	  axis Skill1, Skill2, Skill3
   215	  curve Team1{3,4,5}
   216	  curve Team2{4,3,4}
   217	```
   218	
   219	### Treemap
   220	Hierarchical proportions.
   221	
   222	**Syntax:**
   223	```
   224	treemap-beta
   225	  "Root"
   226	    "Category A"
   227	      "Item 1": 100
   228	      "Item 2": 200
   229	```
   230	
   231	## Technical Diagrams
   232	
   233	### Git Graph
   234	Branching strategies, workflows.
   235	
   236	**Syntax:**
   237	```
   238	gitGraph
   239	  commit
   240	  branch develop
   241	  checkout develop
   242	  commit
   243	  checkout main
   244	  merge develop
   245	```
   246	
   247	### Timeline
   248	Chronological events, milestones.
   249	
   250	**Syntax:**
   251	```
   252	timeline
   253	  2024 : Event A : Event B
   254	  2025 : Event C
   255	```
   256	
   257	### Packet Diagram
   258	Network protocols, structures.
   259	
   260	**Syntax:**
   261	```
   262	packet-beta
   263	  0-15: "Header"
   264	  16-31: "Data"
   265	```
   266	
   267	### ZenUML Sequence
   268	Alternative sequence syntax.
   269	
   270	**Syntax:**
   271	```
   272	zenuml
   273	  A.method() {
   274	    B.process()
   275	    return result
   276	  }
   277	```
   278	
   279	### Mindmap
   280	Brainstorming, hierarchies.
   281	
   282	**Syntax:**
   283	```
   284	mindmap
   285	  root((Central Idea))
   286	    Branch 1
   287	      Sub 1
   288	      Sub 2
   289	    Branch 2
   290	```
   291	
   292	### Requirement Diagram
   293	SysML requirements, traceability.
   294	
   295	**Syntax:**
   296	```
   297	requirementDiagram
   298	  requirement req1 {
   299	    id: R1
   300	    text: User shall login
   301	    risk: Medium
   302	  }
   303	```
   304	
   305	## Quick Reference
   306	
   307	| Type | Best For | Complexity |
   308	|------|----------|------------|
   309	| Flowchart | Processes | Low |
   310	| Sequence | Interactions | Medium |
   311	| Class | OOP | High |
   312	| State | Behaviors | Medium |
   313	| ER | Databases | Low |
   314	| Gantt | Timelines | Medium |
   315	| Architecture | Systems | High |

1	# Mermaid.js Configuration & Theming
     2	
     3	Configuration options, theming, and customization for Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Configuration Methods
     6	
     7	**1. Site-wide Initialization:**
     8	```javascript
     9	mermaid.initialize({
    10	  theme: 'dark',
    11	  startOnLoad: true,
    12	  securityLevel: 'strict',
    13	  fontFamily: 'Arial'
    14	});
    15	```
    16	
    17	**2. Diagram-level Frontmatter:**
    18	````markdown
    19	```mermaid
    20	---
    21	theme: forest
    22	look: handDrawn
    23	---
    24	flowchart TD
    25	  A --> B
    26	```
    27	````
    28	
    29	**3. Configuration Hierarchy:**
    30	Default config → Site config → Diagram config (highest priority)
    31	
    32	## Core Options
    33	
    34	**Rendering:**
    35	- `startOnLoad`: Auto-render on page load (default: true)
    36	- `securityLevel`: "strict" (default), "loose", "antiscript", "sandbox"
    37	- `deterministicIds`: Reproducible SVG IDs (default: false)
    38	- `maxTextSize`: Max diagram text (default: 50000)
    39	- `maxEdges`: Max drawable edges (default: 500)
    40	
    41	**Visual Style:**
    42	- `look`: "classic" (default), "handDrawn"
    43	- `handDrawnSeed`: Numeric seed for hand-drawn consistency
    44	- `darkMode`: Boolean toggle
    45	
    46	**Typography:**
    47	- `fontFamily`: "trebuchet ms, verdana, arial, sans-serif" (default)
    48	- `fontSize`: Base text size (default: 16)
    49	
    50	**Layout:**
    51	- `layout`: "dagre" (default), "elk", "tidy-tree", "cose-bilkent"
    52	
    53	**Debug:**
    54	- `logLevel`: 0-5 from trace to fatal
    55	- `htmlLabels`: Enable HTML in labels (default: false)
    56	
    57	## Theming
    58	
    59	**Built-in Themes:**

1	# Mermaid.js CLI Usage
     2	
     3	Command-line interface for converting Mermaid diagrams to SVG/PNG/PDF.
     4	
     5	## Installation
     6	
     7	**Global Install:**
     8	```bash
     9	npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
    10	```
    11	
    12	**Local Install:**
    13	```bash
    14	npm install @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
    15	./node_modules/.bin/mmdc -h
    16	```
    17	
    18	**No Install (npx):**
    19	```bash
    20	npx -p @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli mmdc -h
    21	```
    22	
    23	**Docker:**
    24	```bash
    25	docker pull ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli
    26	```
    27	
    28	**Requirements:** Node.js ^18.19 || >=20.0
    29	
    30	## Basic Commands
    31	
    32	**Convert to SVG:**
    33	```bash
    34	mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.svg
    35	```
    36	
    37	**Convert to PNG:**
    38	```bash
    39	mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png
    40	```
    41	
    42	**Convert to PDF:**
    43	```bash
    44	mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.pdf
    45	```
    46	
    47	Output format determined by file extension.
    48	
    49	## CLI Flags
    50	
    51	**Core Options:**
    52	- `-i, --input <file>` - Input file (use `-` for stdin)
    53	- `-o, --output <file>` - Output file path
    54	- `-t, --theme <name>` - Theme: default, dark, forest, neutral
    55	- `-b, --background <color>` - Background: transparent, white, #hex
    56	- `--cssFile <file>` - Custom CSS for styling
    57	- `--configFile <file>` - Mermaid configuration file
    58	- `-h, --help` - Show all options
    59	
    60	**Example with All Options:**
    61	```bash
    62	mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o output.png \
    63	  -t dark \
    64	  -b transparent \
    65	  --cssFile custom.css \
    66	  --configFile mermaid-config.json
    67	```
    68	
    69	## Advanced Usage
    70	
    71	**Stdin Piping:**
    72	```bash
    73	cat diagram.mmd | mmdc --input - -o output.svg
    74	
    75	# Or inline
    76	cat << EOF | mmdc --input - -o output.svg
    77	graph TD
    78	  A[Start] --> B[End]
    79	EOF
    80	```
    81	
    82	**Batch Processing:**
    83	```bash
    84	for file in *.mmd; do
    85	  mmdc -i "$file" -o "${file%.mmd}.svg"
    86	done
    87	```
    88	
    89	**Markdown Files:**
    90	Process markdown with embedded diagrams:
    91	```bash
    92	mmdc -i README.template.md -o README.md
    93	```
    94	
    95	## Docker Workflows
    96	
    97	**Basic Docker Usage:**
    98	```bash
    99	docker run --rm \
   100	  -u $(id -u):$(id -g) \
   101	  -v /path/to/diagrams:/data \
   102	  ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli \
   103	  -i diagram.mmd -o output.svg

   105

   107	```bash

   121	## Configuration Files

   124	```json

   126	  "theme": "dark",
   127	  "look": "handDrawn",
   128	  "fontFamily": "Arial",
   129	  "flowchart": {
   130	    "curve": "basis"

   156	## Node.js API

   162	await run('input.mmd', 'output.svg', {
   163	  theme: 'dark',
   164	  backgroundColor: 'transparent'

   167	
   168	**With Options:**

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime
import json

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Parse milestones
def parse_milestones(key, track_name, color, marker):
    items = []
    for item in data[key]['data']:
        dt = datetime.strptime(item['date'], '%Y-%m')
        sig = item['significance']
        size = 80 if sig == 'medium' else 140 if sig == 'high' else 220
        items.append({
            'date': dt,
            'label': item['label'],
            'significance': sig,
            'size': size,
            'track': track_name,
            'color': color,
            'marker': marker
        })
    return items

research = parse_milestones('research_milestones', 'Research', '#1f77b4', 'o')
industry = parse_milestones('industry_milestones', 'Industry', '#ff7f0e', 's')
regulation = parse_milestones('regulation_milestones', 'Regulation', '#d62728', 'D')

# Investment data
investment = data['ai_investment']['data']
inv_years = [datetime(year=d['year'], month=6, day=1) for d in investment]
inv_values = [d['investment'] for d in investment]

# Setup figure
fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(20, 12))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#fafafa')
ax1.set_facecolor('#fafafa')

# Y-positions for tracks
tracks = {'Research': 3, 'Industry': 2, 'Regulation': 1}

# Draw horizontal track lines
for name, y in tracks.items():
    ax1.axhline(y=y, color='#cccccc', linewidth=1, zorder=1)

# Plot milestones
all_milestones = research + industry + regulation
for m in all_milestones:
    y = tracks[m['track']]
    ax1.scatter(m['date'], y, s=m['size'], c=m['color'], marker=m['marker'],
                edgecolors='white', linewidths=1.5, zorder=5, alpha=0.9)

# Annotate critical milestones
annotations = {
    'Transformer architecture': ('2017-06', 'Transformer\n(2017)', 3.35),
    'ChatGPT launches': ('2022-11', 'ChatGPT\n(Nov 2022)', 2.35),
    'EU AI Act agreed': ('2023-05', 'EU AI Act\n(May 2023)', 1.35),
    'Biden Executive Order on AI': ('2023-10', 'Biden EO\n(Oct 2023)', 1.35),
    'Bletchley Declaration': ('2023-11', 'Bletchley\n(Nov 2023)', 1.35),
}

for m in all_milestones:
    label = m['label']
    if label in annotations:
        text, _, y_offset = annotations[label]
        ax1.annotate(annotations[label][1],
                     xy=(m['date'], tracks[m['track']]),
                     xytext=(0, 25 if m['track'] != 'Regulation' else -35),
                     textcoords='offset points',
                     fontsize=9, fontweight='bold',
                     ha='center', va='bottom' if m['track'] != 'Regulation' else 'top',
                     color=m['color'],
                     arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=m['color'], lw=1) if m['track'] == 'Regulation' else None)

# Track labels
for name, y in tracks.items():
    ax1.text(datetime(2009, 6, 1), y, name, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold',
             ha='right', va='center', color='#333333')

# Investment overlay on secondary axis
ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.fill_between(inv_years, inv_values, alpha=0.15, color='#2ca02c', zorder=2)
ax2.plot(inv_years, inv_values, color='#2ca02c', linewidth=2.5, zorder=3, label='AI Investment ($B)')
ax2.set_ylabel('Global Private AI Investment (Billion USD)', fontsize=12, color='#2ca02c', fontweight='bold')
ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#2ca02c')
ax2.set_ylim(0, 140)

# Annotate investment key points
ax2.annotate('$48B\n(2022)', xy=(datetime(2022, 6, 1), 48.2), xytext=(datetime(2021, 3, 1), 65),
             fontsize=9, color='#2ca02c', fontweight='bold',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#2ca02c', lw=1.2))
ax2.annotate('$96B\n(2024)', xy=(datetime(2024, 6, 1), 95.8), xytext=(datetime(2024, 6, 1), 115),
             fontsize=9, color='#2ca02c', fontweight='bold',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#2ca02c', lw=1.2))

# Lag arrows / annotations
ax1.annotate('', xy=(datetime(2022, 11, 1), 2.15), xytext=(datetime(2017, 6, 1), 2.85),
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='#666666', lw=1.5, ls='--'))
ax1.text(datetime(2019, 10, 1), 2.65, '5.4 yr lag', fontsize=9, color='#666666', ha='center', style='italic')

ax1.annotate('', xy=(datetime(2023, 5, 1), 1.15), xytext=(datetime(2022, 11, 1), 1.85),
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='#666666', lw=1.5, ls='--'))
ax1.text(datetime(2023, 2, 1), 1.65, '1.3 yr lag', fontsize=9, color='#666666', ha='center', style='italic')

# Highlight ChatGPT inflection zone
ax1.axvspan(datetime(2022, 10, 1), datetime(2024, 2, 1), alpha=0.06, color='purple', zorder=0)
ax1.text(datetime(2023, 6, 1), 3.6, 'ChatGPT Inflection: 14 months → Biden EO, EU AI Act, Bletchley Declaration',
         fontsize=10, color='#6a1b9a', ha='center', fontweight='bold', style='italic')

# Density annotation
ax1.text(datetime(2015, 1, 1), 0.45, '2010-2017: 14 milestones total  →', fontsize=9, color='#555555', ha='center')
ax1.text(datetime(2023, 6, 1), 0.45, '← 2023-2024: 15+ milestones total', fontsize=9, color='#555555', ha='center', fontweight='bold')

# Axis formatting
ax1.set_xlim(datetime(2009, 6, 1), datetime(2025, 8, 1))
ax1.set_ylim(0.3, 3.8)
ax1.set_yticks([])
ax1.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator())
ax1.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%Y'))
ax1.xaxis.set_minor_locator(mdates.MonthLocator(interval=6))
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=11)
ax1.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Title
fig.suptitle('The Acceleration of AI: Research, Industry & Regulation (2010-2025)',
             fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', color='#1a1a1a', y=0.98)
ax1.set_title('Investment surged from $48B (2022) to $96B (2024) as regulation compressed from years to months',
              fontsize=12, color='#444444', pad=15)

# Legend
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#1f77b4', markersize=10, label='Research'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='s', color='w', markerfacecolor='#ff7f0e', markersize=10, label='Industry'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='D', color='w', markerfacecolor='#d62728', markersize=10, label='Regulation'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color='#2ca02c', linewidth=2.5, label='AI Investment ($B)'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#888888', markersize=6, label='Medium significance'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#888888', markersize=10, label='High significance'),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#888888', markersize=14, label='Critical significance'),
]
ax1.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper left', fontsize=9, framealpha=0.9,
           edgecolor='#cccccc', title='Tracks & Significance', title_fontsize=10)

# Grid
ax1.grid(axis='x', linestyle=':', alpha=0.4, color='#999999')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa')
plt.close()
print('Saved /app/output/result.png')
